sources.notes: E4 is borderline. The test's null is explicitly 'same distribution', and p-values are computed, stored and published to Stability Arena. But the paper gives no numeric alpha or e-value threshold, only 'a predetermined threshold'. A stricter reader may code E4 false, which would put the distance at 3. E3 is false because the paper measures no spread on identical weights to grade against. It mentions within-fingerprint spread terms only inside the energy statistic, and treats infrastructure nondeterminism as a caveat, not a calibrated floor. Some controlled validations are between different models (Qwen to Llama) rather than self-comparisons. The quantization case (BF16 to INT8 of the same weights) and ongoing endpoint monitoring are self-comparisons. The paper also keeps an audit log of change events in a postgres database, with no chaining described (not assigned C2). Nearest lead is B3IT (Chauvin et al.), which uses border inputs, near-tied top tokens at low temperature, as a hypothesis test for LLM API change. It may involve token-level probabilities.
